THE SAME SUCCESS. DIFFERENT INFERENCES.

Read the evidence, then the claim.

Hypothetical cases

CASE 01

Fewer interruptions.
A larger claim.

A district introduces phone storage to reduce interruptions and support learning. Staff observations document fewer interruptions during lessons.

THE IMPLEMENTATION REPORT

“Interruptions have fallen. The policy has improved learning.”

The leadership team cites the improvement as its reason for canceling a planned review of student learning.

WHAT THE CASE SUPPORTS

A benefit is established.
The learning claim is not.

Fewer interruptions support a claim about classroom conditions. They do not, alone, establish retention, transfer, or better understanding.

An illustration of the proposed mechanism

All four conditions are stipulated in this fictional case. A real study would need evidence connecting the improvement, its interpretation, and the decision to stop asking.

?
What evidence would change this judgment?

Look for the original learning purpose, credible measures of interruptions, and records showing why the learning review was canceled.
